P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but notes not read back: 'I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like an overview as well.' The standing three-part frame was delivered twice, once before the prospect's phone died and again on his return, and both times without what's in the way or what you need. No agreement was sought either time — the rep went from 'if not that's fine as well alrighty' straight into the open question, which was itself asked well: 'I guess from your perspective what was it that you were hoping we could potentially help you out with.'

P2.evidence: Better than most in this folder but still half-run. Current training was asked directly — 'walk me through what you're doing now, are you training with kettlebells now?' — producing the reel circuit, the weights used and the running mileage. Results were probed rather than accepted: 'And like, so you've lost 60 pounds already?' Diet and lifestyle were opened properly with 'what would you say your lifestyle is like now?', which surfaced the strict-versus-lenient oscillation and the cravings. But age and weight were volunteered, height was never taken, and — on a call that reached a close attempt — no health conditions, no injuries, no chronic pain, no sleep and no energy were ever asked about. A prospect who was 260 lb a year ago and has dropped 60 warrants a health question on its own.

P3.evidence: Among the best goals work in the corpus. The vague opening want was refused and pushed on twice — 'What, what does that, what does that actually look like for you?' — until it produced something concrete. The six-month question was asked properly and then sharpened into the deep question: 'What's different at that point? Because you're showing up as a different person then... What actually changes for you?', producing confidence, credibility and the ability to guide people. Legacy and identity were driven through cleanly. And the reflect-back ran textbook: 'sounds like this is a lot more than just swinging some kettlebells around for you, huh?... It sounds like it's more about who you can become' / 'Yeah, yeah, and that's what I see it as... shedding off the old me.' The nephews were volunteered rather than drawn out with a who-else-does-this-impact question, and nothing physical-he-cannot-do-now was asked.

P4.evidence: The past-attempts questions themselves were skipped — the 60 lb loss and the earlier strength-training phase both surfaced without being asked for. But the root-cause half was executed properly. 'My next question was going to be, what takes you out of the zone?' is a clean P4c. The unscripted scaling sequence did the rest of the work better than the script would have: 'let's say the best version of you is a 10 out of 10, where would you put yourself now?' followed by 'What do you feel like you need to go to a 10?', which had the prospect name the gap himself — 'I need a routine... I have the motivation but I think it's just the routine and the direction.' The rep then ran a strong P4f inversion, establishing that effort was never the problem: 'You've lost 60 pounds... you have the ability to push through hard things. You've got the ability to be consistent. You've got the motivation for it... So the results are inevitable, brother.'

P5.evidence: The sixth consecutive call in this folder with no consequence frame at all. No two-year picture, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not'. The readiness question ran and ran well — 'do you feel like you're ready for that? And do you feel like you're ready to step into those shoes is the question?' The cost of this omission is now measurable across the batch: the price objection arrives with nothing on the other side of the scale, and it arrived here at 00:34:34.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions were asked before any number was spoken, which is the correct sequence and the one this rep gets right more often than not. 'do you believe it's possible to get where you want to go?' — answered yes with reasoning. Then the right-person half: 'do you feel like with what you've seen from Trevor, like he can be somebody to help you get to that point?' — 'Oh yeah, for sure.' A clear yes was obtained before the offer walkthrough began. The specific all-in question, whether there is any reason he would not go all in given everything he needed, was never asked, and it is the one that would have surfaced the payment question thirteen minutes earlier than it did.

P11.evidence: Unreachable within the recording. The rep had described the onboarding sequence in advance and asked which tier the prospect leaned toward, but the recording ends at 00:35:00 before any payment, booking, agreement or welcome step could occur. This is a recording artefact rather than an established omission and should not be read as a rep failure.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger present and unambiguous at 00:34:34 — 'I'd have to see because 6K, yeah' — preceded twenty seconds earlier by the instalment question, 'is it like one flat rate at one time, or is it like a process of through, like, bi-weekly or is it weekly?' The only observable response is the standard credit-card framing, which is not an OC move. No isolation, no should-I-versus-how, no financial picture, and no payment plan offered even though the prospect had explicitly asked whether one existed. Scored miss on what is demonstrable, with an important qualification: the recording ends roughly twenty-six seconds after the trigger, so this is not evidence that the play was not run, it is evidence that it cannot be observed. See the data_integrity flag. One point of partial credit the rep does earn — he pre-framed the money objection during the comfort-zone answer at 00:29:51, listing 'the program's too much money' among the reasons a mind manufactures to avoid change.

A prospect who has already succeeded once, unaided and for free — the cheaper-alternative gap in its most flattering form, since the cheaper alternative here was his own discipline. There is no scripted play for it. The rep's improvised handling was the strongest in the batch and did not require discounting: he converted the prior success from an objection into the evidence base for the purchase. 'You've lost 60 pounds. That's impressive stuff... what I want to take away from that is that you have the ability.' That reframe turns sixty pounds of self-directed proof into a reason the coaching will work rather than a reason it is unnecessary, and the prospect closed the loop himself: 'I just need the direction. I just need someone to tell me where to.' Worth extracting into the playbook.

notes: Process-wise the best call in the batch. Phases 3, 4 and 6 all landed, the reflect-back was textbook, and the unscripted ten-out-of-ten scaling question outperformed the scripted alternatives by getting the prospect to name the product's value proposition in his own words. Conduct was clean and included an unprompted downward price correction. Two things to coach. First, the consequence frame, absent for the sixth call running — with P5 built, a prospect this bought-in does not arrive at the number cold. Second, baseline: no health, injury, sleep or energy question was asked of a man who has lost sixty pounds in a year and is about to start ballistic loading. Separately, and not a coaching matter: this call's outcome cannot be determined from the file and should be re-sourced before it enters any close-rate calculation.
